statement: You have a two-pan balance and four weights of 1 g, 3 g, 9 g and 27 g. Any weights may go on either pan, next to the object or opposite it. How many different whole-number masses, starting from 1 g, can be measured exactly in a single weighing?

choices.misconception: I put weights only on the pan opposite the object, so I counted only the sums of the weights.
I counted every way of placing each weight on the left, on the right or off the balance.
I counted every placement except all weights off, without noticing each mass is reached by two mirror-image placements.
I counted zero as one of the masses, as if weighing nothing counted.

hints: A weight next to the object counts as a negative.

Each weight can be added, subtracted or left out, so the measured mass is a sum of plus or minus the weights. Find the largest mass possible and ask whether every whole number below it can be reached.
The largest mass is 1 + 3 + 9 + 27 = 40. Check that small cases such as 2 = 3 - 1 and 5 = 9 - 3 - 1 work.

solutions.reliable: A weight opposite the object adds its mass and one beside the object subtracts it, so the object's mass is a sum where each of 1, 3, 9, 27 appears with +, - or not at all. The largest is 40. Every value from 1 to 40 can be made: 1, 3 - 1, 3, 3 + 1, 9 - 3 - 1, and so on, since with 1 and 3 you reach every mass from 1 to 4, adding 9 extends this to every mass up to 13, and adding 27 extends it to 40. So 40 masses. The transferable idea: when each item can be used positively, negatively or not at all, powers of 3 cover every whole number up to their total.
solutions.elegant: There are 3 to the power 4 = 81 placements. One gives 0, and the other 80 split into mirror pairs giving m and -m, so at most 40 positive masses, and since every value from 1 to 40 is reached, the answer is 40. The transferable idea: count placements, then divide out the symmetry.

whyOnTest: Balance puzzles test whether you allow weights on both pans, which turns a doubling count into a powers-of-three count.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
